groups: FX: any number (each track its own)
FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)

items.label: ANALOG 2 (analog-style synth, swarm, 2 filters)
items.desc: The main subtractive synth: two oscillators with hard sync, a swarm of up to 6 detuned copies (supersaw), two filters. About 6 KB of flash and 4.7 KB of fast RAM code; it is also the stand-in that most other engines fall back to, so keep it unless you need the space.

items.label: ANALOG 2 filter: LADR (transistor ladder, Moog-style)
items.desc: A 4-pole transistor ladder: a tanh at its input (drive grits it), the bass thinning as RES rises, ringing in tune at the top of RES. FTYP as the Oberheim Xpander's mixes of its four stages. FLT 2 gets a MODEL card next to FTYP (LP12 LP24 BP HP NOTCH), on an ANALOG track only. A sound that asks for a model this build leaves out plays ANALOG 2's own filter in the same mode. Floating point (the FPU), about 3x the CPU of ANALOG 2's own filter on the host per voice, not measured on the FM-1 yet.
items.tested: host-tested only (responses, self-oscillation, stability), not on a device

items.label: ANALOG 2 filter: OTA (IR3109 4-pole, Juno-style)
items.desc: A 4-pole OTA ladder: the input stays clean and the passband is made up as RES rises, the resonance saturates on its own path: creamy, its self-oscillation round. FTYP as the Xpander's mixes. FLT 2 gets a MODEL card next to FTYP (LP12 LP24 BP HP NOTCH), on an ANALOG track only. A sound that asks for a model this build leaves out plays ANALOG 2's own filter in the same mode. Floating point (the FPU), about 3x the CPU of ANALOG 2's own filter on the host per voice, not measured on the FM-1 yet.
items.tested: host-tested only (responses, self-oscillation, stability), not on a device

items.label: ANALOG 2 filter: DIOD (diode ladder, 303-style)
items.desc: A diode ladder: four coupled stages, each loading the one before, solved exactly every 16 samples, a tanh at its input: squelchy, a thin vocal resonance that rings at the cutoff. FLT 2 gets a MODEL card next to FTYP (LP12 LP24 BP HP NOTCH), on an ANALOG track only. A sound that asks for a model this build leaves out plays ANALOG 2's own filter in the same mode. Floating point (the FPU), about 3x the CPU of ANALOG 2's own filter on the host per voice, not measured on the FM-1 yet.
items.tested: host-tested only (responses, self-oscillation, stability), not on a device

items.label: ANALOG 2 filter: MS20 (Sallen-Key, MS-20-style)
items.desc: A Sallen-Key 2-pole with its band fed back through a tanh: it screams at high RES and rings loud. LP, BP, HP and NOTCH its own, LP24 a further pole (18 dB). FLT 2 gets a MODEL card next to FTYP (LP12 LP24 BP HP NOTCH), on an ANALOG track only. A sound that asks for a model this build leaves out plays ANALOG 2's own filter in the same mode. Floating point (the FPU), about 3x the CPU of ANALOG 2's own filter on the host per voice, not measured on the FM-1 yet.
items.tested: host-tested only (responses, self-oscillation, stability), not on a device

items.label: DIGITAL (4-operator FM)
items.desc: Four-operator FM synth: 8 classic algorithms, feedback on operator 4 and one modulation INDEX with its own envelope. About 2 KB of flash; the stand-in for FM6 when FM6 is left out.

items.label: PHASE (phase distortion)
items.desc: Phase-distortion synth: bends the phase of a cosine wave to get saw, square, pulse and resonant shapes with a second line to mix or ring-modulate. About 1.4 KB of flash; the stand-in for CZ.

items.label: PHASE: FOLD (a sine wavefolder on E7)
items.desc: PHASE's last EDIT knob (E7, empty until now) becomes FOLD: a sine wavefolder on the voice, after the two lines and before SUB. 0 is off (the sound as before); up from 0 a soft saturation, then up to four folds. Above A4 it folds less, so the top notes alias less. Turning it on or off mid-note crossfades, no click. About 0.8 KB.
items.notice: From Felucca-Engines' PHASE FOLD by Leo Kuroshita (hugelton/Felucca-Engines 04ffe90, MIT). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: LOFI (chip sounds, wavetable)
items.desc: Chip voice: pulse, triangle, saw, noise and a 4-bit wavetable, with a few-bit amplitude, a held (low) sample rate and a pitch sweep. About 2 KB of flash.

items.label: SAMPLE (sample sets, USR slots)
items.desc: Plays the built-in sample sets and your own samples (USR1..USR3 slots) across the keyboard, with loops. About 1.4 KB of flash plus the sets you keep (see Sample sets); it is also the stand-in for GRAIN and SLICE.

items.label: VOICE (formant, sung vowels)
items.desc: Formant synth that sings vowels from the keyboard (4 voices; BUZZ and BREATH shape the voice). About 2.7 KB of flash; a special sound, leave it out if you need the space.

items.label: TRIO (3 oscillators)
items.desc: Three oscillators with ring modulation and hard sync into a multimode filter, in the style of early 8-bit home-computer sound chips. About 3.4 KB of flash.

items.label: WHEEL (drawbar organ)
items.desc: Tonewheel-style organ: nine sine drawbars per note, 16 registrations to choose from. About 2.3 KB of flash and 2.5 KB of RAM.

items.label: GRAIN (granular on the sample sets)
items.desc: Granular synth: plays clouds of tiny grains cut from the sample sets or your USR slots. About 4.9 KB of flash and 21 KB of pool; with no sample set built it plays your USR samples only.

items.label: FM6 (DX7, bit-exact with Dexed)
items.desc: Six-operator FM that plays Yamaha DX7 voices the way the Dexed plug-in does (MSFA, bit for bit), with its own operator editor and DX7 SysEx in; INIT VOICE and the voice packs below are its sounds. The biggest engine: about 28 KB of flash and 6 KB of RAM; its options below trim it down.

items.label: FM6 operator editor on the black keys
items.desc: Edit a DX7 voice on the device: hold ENV and press a black key to pick an operator, the pitch envelope or the global page, then turn the knobs. About 6.3 KB of flash; off: a voice can only be replaced by DX7 SysEx.

items.label: FM6 DX7 SysEx in (a voice, a 32-voice bank)
items.desc: Receives DX7 SysEx over USB MIDI, from Dexed or any DX7 librarian: a single voice replaces the selected FM6 track's voice (then SAVE AS keeps it as a user preset), a 32-voice bank becomes a pick list at the end of that track's PRESETS (RAM only, until power-off) to audition and SAVE AS. Nothing is sent back. About 1.3 KB of flash and 4.3 KB of pool RAM for the frame buffers.

items.label: FM6 voice pack: keys and e-pianos (16)
items.desc: 16 voices of my own for the FM6 track, listed in its PRESETS after the user presets (K01..K16): electric pianos, clavs, organs, a harpsichord. About 2.0-2.3 KB of flash.

items.label: FM6 voice pack: basses (16)
items.desc: 16 bass voices for the FM6 track, listed in its PRESETS after the user presets (B01..B16): slap, fretless, synth, pluck and sub basses. About 2.0-2.3 KB of flash.

items.label: FM6 voice pack: bells and mallets (16)
items.desc: 16 voices for the FM6 track, listed in its PRESETS after the user presets (M01..M16): bells, marimba, vibes, kalimba, steel drum, glass and chimes. About 2.0-2.3 KB of flash.

items.label: FM6 voice pack: pads, leads, brass and FX (16)
items.desc: 16 voices for the FM6 track, listed in its PRESETS after the user presets (P01..P16): pads, leads, brass, strings and effect sounds. About 2.0-2.3 KB of flash.

items.label: FM6 voice pack: 80s mega classics (16)
items.desc: 16 recreations of the famous 80s DX sounds (the e-piano, the bass, the bells, the brass, the marimba, the harmonica ...) for the FM6 track, listed in its PRESETS after the user presets (801..816). All programmed from scratch, none copied from a ROM or a cartridge. About 2.0-2.3 KB of flash.

items.label: CZ native tone collection in PRESETS
items.desc: With CZ built, a CZ track's PRESETS list ends with a collection of 26 CZ-1 tones (the web editor imports and exports Casio .syx). Loading one sets only the engine's values: the track keeps its FX, mix and pattern. The collection takes 8 KiB at USR3's end (USR3 holds that much less). About 2 KB of flash with CZ (measured); no RAM. (The FM6 user bank U01..U32 that this item once listed went 2026-10-18; FM6's own list is its voice packs and a received DX7 bank, with FM6_SYSEX or a pack.)

items.label: SLICE (break slicer + its BREAK sample)
items.desc: Break slicer: cuts a loop (the built-in BREAK, 22 KB of samples, or a USR slot) into 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 slices or one per hit and plays them from the keys or the sequencer. About 27 KB of flash and 6 KB of RAM; off by default.

items.label: DRONE (drones, ambient, binaural beats)
items.desc: A coupled network for drones and ambient (engine 16), after Caravel's DRONE (bonszaimusic), itself inspired by the LYRA-8: four sines a note, each phase-modulating another (COUPLE) as PAIRS, a CHAIN or a RING (TOPO), SPREAD from unison to 1 : 5/4 : 3/2 : 2, a soft cubic CHAR, a slow DRIFT and a one-pole TONE; the track's DTUNE detunes the four. BEAT plays binaural beats: each ear its own pitch, 0.05 to 40 Hz apart (headphones; the network runs twice). HOLD latches the keys. 9 presets (theta, alpha, delta and gamma beats among them); one voice a part, about half an 8-note ANALOG part's CPU (host-measured).
items.provenance_line: Caravel 0.3.3 (bonszaimusic/caravel, a Felucca fork) @ c6c61c7 by bonszaimusic (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: PLAITS (Plaits' waveshaping, additive, granular formant, particles)
items.desc: Four of Mutable Instruments Plaits' synthesis models as one engine (engine 17), with Plaits' own controls: MODEL, HARMONICS, TIMBRE, MORPH. WAVSH: a slope through five waveshapers and a wavefolder; ADDTV: 24 harmonics under a moving bump spectrum (AUX: an 8-drawbar organ); GRFMT: two synced formant grainlets (AUX: the Z oscillator); PRTCL: random pings of six resonant filters (rain, droplets, dust). AUX fades to each model's second output, TONE and LPG are a low-pass gate, VEL lets the velocity open TIMBRE. 12 presets; 4 voices a part, about twice an ANALOG voice's CPU (host-measured; PRTCL the heaviest). Integer code, no float. About 11 KB of flash (its tables 3.6 KB), no RAM of its own: its state lives in the part memory the other engines share.
items.notice: Plaits' models by Emilie Gillet (pichenettes/eurorack f4cfa76, MIT), ported to integers. Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.
items.provenance_line: Mutable Instruments Plaits (pichenettes/eurorack) @ f4cfa76 by Emilie Gillet (MIT)

items.label: STRINGS (a 1970s string machine)
items.desc: Clipper's string machine (engine 18), after the Solina, ARP and Elka ensembles: 16', 8' and 4' registers divided down from one phase, so they stay locked; a three-line ensemble whose taps two LFOs move 120 degrees apart (ENS, RATE); SHP turns the saws toward squares; a 12 dB low-pass (CUT, RES). 16 presets. Integer code, about 2.5 KB of flash.
items.notice: From Clipper by 3dSam (isod89/clipper-fm1, GPL-3.0-only). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: VPS (vector phaseshaping)
items.desc: Clipper's vector phaseshaping (engine 19, after Kleimola et al., DAFx 2011): a sine read through a bent phase. D moves the bend along the period, V sets its height: below 1 a phase-distorted, CZ-like wave, above 1 a formant at V times the note (VENV sweeps it with each note). OSC2 a second one, mirrored and detuned (DTN), SUB a sine an octave down, then a 12 dB low-pass. 10 presets. Integer code, no table: about 2 KB of flash.
items.notice: From Clipper by 3dSam (isod89/clipper-fm1, GPL-3.0-only). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: TERRAIN (wave terrain)
items.desc: Clipper's wave terrain synthesis (engine 20): an orbit circles over one of 8 surfaces (TERR) once a period of the note, the surface's height under it is the sound. RAD, X and Y place the orbit, ORB squeezes it to a line or turns it into a figure eight, DRIFT moves its centre slowly, each note its own way. Then a 12 dB low-pass. 10 presets. Integer code; about 18 KB of flash, the surfaces 16 KB of it.
items.notice: From Clipper by 3dSam (isod89/clipper-fm1, GPL-3.0-only). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: WSEQ (wave sequencing)
items.desc: Clipper's wave sequencing (engine 21), after the Korg Wavestation: each note plays one of 16 sequences (SEQ) of up to 16 steps, each its own wave, pitch and level, at the song's tempo (RATE 1/32 to a bar). XFADE fades each step into the next, LOOP plays forward, back, ping-pong or once, START picks the first step, PITCH scales the steps' intervals. Then a 12 dB low-pass. 16 presets. Integer code, the waves computed: about 5 KB of flash.
items.notice: From Clipper by 3dSam (isod89/clipper-fm1, GPL-3.0-only). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: VECTOR (Prophet VS-style vector synthesis)
items.desc: Clipper's vector synthesis (engine 22), after the Prophet VS and the Wavestation's joystick: four of 16 single-cycle waves at the corners of a square (A B C D), a point in it (X, Y) mixing them; MOVE sends the point round a circle, a figure eight, the square's edge, a sweep from A or a random walk, slow or fast. Then a 12 dB low-pass. 16 presets. Integer code; about 24 KB of flash, the waves 21 KB of it.
items.notice: From Clipper by 3dSam (isod89/clipper-fm1, GPL-3.0-only). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: WAVE (Clipper's wavetables)
items.desc: Clipper's wavetable engine (engine 25): 8 of its tables (TABL) of 16 single-cycle frames, POS sweeping through them crossfaded (PPG / Serum style; the track's SHP moves POS), a second oscillator DTN cents up, a SUB sine, then a 12 dB low-pass with drive (CUT RES DRV KTR). Without aliasing: the tables are spectra, the main loop builds one table's band-limited copies in the pool, and every WAVE track plays that one table (the first WAVE track's TABL). 13 presets. Integer code; about 70 KB of flash (the spectra 64 KB) and 72 KB of the pool: a build with it needs a shorter delay line.
items.notice: From Clipper by 3dSam (isod89/clipper-fm1, GPL-3.0-only). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: SID (the Commodore 64's MOS 6581 / 8580)
items.desc: Mini-Tone's SID engine (engine 23): one voice of reSID 0.16 in integer code, three a part as the chip has. TRI SAW PULSE NOISE and the combined waveforms sampled from real chips (WAVE), PW, SYNC and RING against a second oscillator RATIO semitones away (MOD), the chip's multimode filter (MODE: LP BP HP and their mixes, CUT on the FC register's curve, RES in its 16 steps) and the 6581 or 8580 (MODEL). 26 presets. Integer code; about 44 KB of flash, reSID's tables 40 KB of it.
items.notice: SID by Stephane Schmitz (Mini-Tone, GPL-3.0-only) after reSID 0.16 by Dag Lem (GPL-2.0-or-later). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

provenance.author: Stephane Schmitz

items.label: PROPHET (a Prophet-5 style voice)
items.desc: A Prophet-5 Rev 4 style voice (engine 24) from Melodee's PROPHET: two oscillators (A: saw, pulse or both, hard-synced to B or not; B: saw, triangle, pulse and their mixes, B FRQ semitones away), the MIX between them, Poly-Mod from B (PMOD: on A's pitch, or on the cutoff) and the Curtis 4-pole (CUT, RES), PW for both pulses. The track's ENV and LFO drive it; 12 presets of our own, no Sequential programs. Five voices. Floating point (the FPU), its own unit; about 11 KB of flash.
items.notice: The voice is Melodee's (Kerem Kilic, GPL-3.0-only), with our controls. Tested in the host tests only, not on a device. Not affiliated with Sequential.

items.label: drum synth: the 32 synthesised kits
items.desc: The drum synth's 32 kits (808-style, 909-style and others), generated by the firmware, so they take no sample memory. One of three drum synths, each on its own: these 32 kits, KAWA, PLAITS. The synth's voice they share (about 9.6 KB of flash) is built with any one of them and counted once (the last one switched off frees it): with KAWA or PLAITS on, the 32 kits cost about 1.5 KB of flash, alone about 11 KB. Not the X0X 909 / 808 kits: those are separate items, with their own samples. The 32 kits also play the sounds an X0X kit lacks (without them, a sampled kit, else KAWA or PLAITS; with none of those, silent). Without them the kit list starts at the first kit built.

items.label: drum synth: KAWA kit (kit 47)
items.desc: A drum synth of its own, the KAWA kit, after Kawa Tracker's kit engine: a guiro, a clap with its hands, a flammed snare, a brush and a shaker that swell in, tight-cluster hats, a ride's bell, ring-modulated toms and cowbell, a kick with an FM beater. Any lane of another kit can borrow its sounds. It adds four cymbal tunings, the second partial ringing or modulating the tone, re-strikes and a rise to the drum synth, used by this kit only (the other kits sound as before). Needs neither the 32 kits nor PLAITS: about 2.2 KB beside them, 12 KB alone (the synth's voice with it). A build without it plays the 808 kit for KAWA (without the 32 kits: the first kit built).
items.notice: From Kawa Tracker's kit engine by Guizmoh (Guizmoh/Kawa-Tracker-Fm1 kawa_drums.c, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: drum synth: PLAITS kit (kit 48), Plaits' kick and snare
items.desc: A drum synth of its own, the PLAITS kit: two kicks and two snares from Mutable Instruments Plaits' synthetic bass drum and snare drum models (a distorted sine with FM and a click; two FM sines with filtered noise), the other lanes the 909's sounds. Any lane of another kit can borrow them. The drum EDIT moves them: TUNE, DECAY, CUT + (their TONE / FM), CLICK (the kick's FM), SNAP (the snare's snap). Integer code with 64-bit products, heavier on the CPU than the other drum sounds. Needs neither the 32 kits nor KAWA: about 4.6 KB beside them, 14 KB alone (the synth's voice with it). A build without it plays the 909 kit for PLAITS (without the 32 kits: the first kit built).
items.notice: Plaits' drum models by Emilie Gillet (MIT), in the integer port of Hortator by Leo Kuroshita and DEADACTIVE (DeadActive/hortator 7e34159, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.
