items.label: X0X 909 kit (circuit-modelled TR-909)
items.desc: X0X's TR-909 drum kit (kit UID 37; the drum models are circuit-modelled, hi-hats, ride and crash are samples), on the 16 lanes; SHAKER, CONGA, COWBELL play the synthesised 909's. Big: about 151 KB of flash (see its cymbal option) and uses floating point. A build without it plays the synthesised 909 for it and keeps the kit
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), itself from 9W9 / 8W8 by athousanddetails and ER-99 by Matthew Cieplak (GPL-3.0); the 808's rim shot after sc808 (Yoshinosuke Horiuchi / Sam Aaron, MIT). Float DSP.

items.label: X0X 909: ride and crash sample quality
items.desc: 8-bit block floating point as before; 6-bit: 22 KB less, 30 dB against the 16-bit source instead of 42 (screens x0xdrums-perf-2026-10-06); off: RIDE and CRASH play the synthesised 909's (the hi-hat samples stay)

items.label: X0X 909: hi-hat sample quality
items.desc: The closed and open hat samples as 8-bit block floating point as before, or 6-bit (four mantissas in three bytes, as the ride and crash's 6-bit): about 5 KB less, 30 dB against the 16-bit source instead of 42 (measured by tools/gen_x0x_drums.py; the 909's own cymbals are 6-bit). No other 909 voice reads a sample

items.label: X0X 909: saturator curve (tanh) resolution
items.desc: The 909's saturators read tanh from a table with linear interpolation: 1024 points as before, or 256 points: 3 KB less, within 1e-4 of tanh (80 dB below the signal), no audible change (tests/x0x_drums_test.c measures it)

items.label: X0X 808 kit (circuit-modelled TR-808)
items.desc: X0X's TR-808 drum kit (kit UID 38; 16 circuit-modelled sounds) on the 16 lanes; MIDI also plays MT, LC, HC and the claves (note 75). About 30 KB of flash and uses floating point. A build without it plays the synthesised 808 for it and keeps the kit
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), itself from 9W9 / 8W8 by athousanddetails and ER-99 by Matthew Cieplak (GPL-3.0); the 808's rim shot after sc808 (Yoshinosuke Horiuchi / Sam Aaron, MIT). Float DSP.

items.label: sampled drums (the PERC set, 99 KB)
items.desc: The recorded drum samples (the PERC set, about 99 KB of flash) behind the five sampled kits below. Switching this off drops all of them; the drum track then needs a drum synth.

items.label: sampled kit ACOUSTIC
items.desc: The sampled kit as recorded (the basic kit of the PERC set). It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: sampled kit DEEP
items.desc: The sampled kit tuned down and softened by a low-pass filter: a darker, heavier kit. It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: sampled kit TIGHT
items.desc: The sampled kit with every hit cut short by a fast decay: a dry, punchy kit. It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: sampled kit BRIGHT
items.desc: The sampled kit tuned two semitones up: a lighter kit. It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: sampled kit DUST
items.desc: The sampled kit tuned slightly down, filtered and reduced to a coarse bit depth: a gritty lo-fi kit. It shares the PERC samples with the other sampled kits, so leaving it out saves no memory (only leaving out all of them does); a project using it plays another kit.

items.label: drum sound editor (EDIT on the drum track)
items.desc: Per-lane sound tweaks over the kit (TUNE, DECAY, SNAP, CLICK, BEND, CUT, DRIVE, LEVEL on synthesised kits; TUNE, DECAY, CUT, LEVEL on sampled ones). About 1.2 KB of flash; off: kits play as they are and saved tweaks are kept but not applied.

items.label: drum EDIT: TUNE on the noise sounds (hats, shaker, clap)
items.desc: On a synthesised kit, a sound with no tone (closed hat, shaker, clap) had nothing for TUNE to move. With this, TUNE moves its filter and its noise high-pass, about a semitone's worth a step, as a resampled sample would sound. A few dozen bytes.
items.notice: From SLOOP 2.8's drum TUNE by isod89 (isod89/sloop-fm1 b77bf55, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: user samples on drum lanes
items.desc: A drum lane can play one of your own samples (a hit of a USR slot, with start and length) instead of the kit's sound. About 1.2 KB of flash; off: such lanes play the kit sound.

items.label: user drum kits (bank of 16 in data flash)
items.desc: Lane sources from other kits and the X0X machines, and a bank of 16 user kits (each lane's source and sound tweaks) saved in flash. About 2.8 KB of flash; off: lanes play the kit as it is.

items.label: PIANO (Steinway, 44 KB)
items.desc: A grand piano, plus the dusty and lo-fi piano variants. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: BASS (39 KB)
items.desc: An upright bass, plus a deep bass variant. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: VIBES (33 KB)
items.desc: A vibraphone. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: HORNS (26 KB)
items.desc: Horn stabs. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: STRINGS (20 KB)
items.desc: String stabs. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: FLUTE (31 KB)
items.desc: A lo-fi flute. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: SCRATCH (23 KB)
items.desc: Turntable scratch hits. Played by the SAMPLE and GRAIN engines (and their presets); leaving it out frees its flash, and it can still be uploaded to a USR slot.

items.label: DIST (per-track drive)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A distortion on each synth track: low cut, drive from 1x to 8x into an asymmetric soft clip, and a tone filter that closes as the drive rises. About 0.4 KB of flash; off: the DIST controls disappear.

items.label: chorus
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The chorus effect, fed by each track's CHO send. About 0.4 KB of flash and 4 KB of pool; off: the CHO sends and the chorus settings disappear.

items.label: delay
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The tempo-synced delay (echo), fed by each track's DLY send. Costs 128 KB of the pool at the full length: shorten it with the length option, or leave it out.

items.label: delay length (how long an echo can be)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The longest delay time, which sets the pool memory the delay takes. A time longer than the line is halved until it fits, so it stays on the beat; shorter lines suit fast tempos only.

items.label: reverb
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The reverb, fed by each track's REV send and the drums' reverb, with its algorithms below (tick at least one). Each one ticked is on the device's FX > REVERB > TYPE and in the web editor's Reverb popup, switched while it plays; with one ticked there is no TYPE. They share one line buffer, sized to the largest. The biggest user of RAM among the FX (about 17 KB with ROOM); off: the REV sends and reverb settings disappear.

items.label: reverb: ROOM
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Four delay lines at 44.1 kHz, the reverb as it always was: sparse for its first ~300 ms (separate echoes, a grainy start), then the tail. Its 17 KB of lines set the shared buffer's size when it is ticked. Off, with another algorithm ticked: about 1.8 KB of flash, 2.4 KB of RAM and 2 KB of pool saved.

items.label: reverb: PLATE (Dattorro)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Dattorro's figure-of-eight plate at 22.05 kHz: dense from ~50 ms, a smooth decay, nothing above ~11 kHz, about 10 % fewer instructions than ROOM. A 16 KB ring (8 KB at half rate) in the shared buffer. Beside ROOM: about 2.9 KB of flash and 3.4 KB of RAM; with two or more algorithms each one's code runs from main RAM. Experimental: measured on the host and in the emulator only, not yet heard on an FM-1.
items.notice: PLATE: measured on the host and in the emulator only; not yet heard on an FM-1.

items.label: reverb: FDN8 (long, lush)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Long and lush: eight slowly modulated lines at 22.05 kHz, dense from ~50 ms, the widest and least ringing tail, nothing above ~11 kHz. Up to SIZE 90 the ROOM's decay; above it the decay doubles every 10 steps to ~14 s at 126 and a near-freeze at 127, the treble kept as DAMP says; about 20 % more instructions than ROOM. A 16 KB ring (8 KB at half rate) in the shared buffer. Beside ROOM: about 4.0 KB of flash and 4.3 KB of RAM (with PLATE too, 1.1 KB of flash and 1.8 KB of RAM are shared). Experimental: measured on the host and in the emulator only, not yet heard on an FM-1.
items.notice: FDN8: measured on the host and in the emulator only; not yet heard on an FM-1.

items.label: reverb: VTINY (Airwindows VerbTiny)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Airwindows' VerbTiny (Chris Johnson, MIT): sixteen lines in four 4 x 4 Householder stages, left and right in one loop, at 22.05 kHz. A plain early-digital texture: peakier and grainier than FDN8 (it is not modulated), dense from ~80 ms, ringing no more than the ROOM; nothing above ~11 kHz. SIZE as the ROOM's decay up to 90, then FDN8's long top (~11 s at 126, a near-freeze at 127); DAMP the ROOM's treble loss. Its lines fill the shared 16 KB ring (8 KB at half rate: a smaller room). About 40 % more instructions than FDN8. Beside ROOM: about 4.5 KB of flash and 6.5 KB of main RAM (the tanks' code runs from RAM), no pool past the shared ring (user-default has no flash left for it). Experimental: measured on the host only, not yet heard on an FM-1.
items.notice: VTINY: measured on the host only; not yet heard on an FM-1.

items.label: reverb buffers in the pool (saves ~17 KB RAM)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Keeps the reverb's shared line buffer (17 KB with ROOM, 8.7 KB at half rate; PLATE and FDN8 without ROOM 16 KB, 8 KB at half rate; SPRING alone 8 KB) in the pool instead of main RAM: main RAM is the scarcer, and the sound and the code stay the same. Needs that much pool free (the undo history shrinks by it in the pool and grows by it in RAM).

items.label: half-rate reverb (half the RAM, no top octave)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Runs the ROOM reverb at half the sample rate (22.05 kHz) behind a half-band filter: its memory takes half the RAM (-8.7 KB) and it costs less CPU, with the same decay and room size. PLATE and FDN8 already run at 22.05 kHz; here they get half the ring (8 KB), a smaller tank with more audible modes. The reverb loses its top octave (above ~11 kHz); the dry sound and the other buses are untouched.

items.label: SLICER (stutter / gate insert)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A tempo-synced 16-step gate or stutter on each track (not the sample slicer engine): chops the sound to a pattern. About 1.2 KB of flash and 32 KB of pool at the full capture length.

items.label: SLICER capture length (stutter memory)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: How much sound each track's stutter records to repeat: the shorter capture saves 16 KB of pool and limits how long a repeated chunk can be (the gate mode is unaffected).

items.label: PUNCH (16 punch-in FX)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Hold FX and press a white key to put the whole mix through one of 16 effects while it is held (loops, reverse, tape stop, half speed, wobble, echo, filters, crush, gate), beat-synced. About 2.3 KB of flash and 64 KB of pool at the full ring.

items.label: PUNCH memory length (how much mix it can loop)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: How much of the mix the loop, reverse, tape-stop and echo effects can capture; the shorter ring saves 32 KB of pool and cuts the longest loop in half.

items.label: DJ filter (MASTER FILT)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: One knob on the master (MASTER > FILT): turn left for a low-pass closing, right for a high-pass opening, centre is off. About 0.7 KB of flash.

items.label: DUST (vinyl / lo-fi master)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: One knob on the master (MASTER > DUST) that runs the mix through an old sampler and a record: drive, lower sample rate, fewer bits, a darker tone, hiss and crackle while playing. About 0.7 KB of flash.

items.label: DUCK (kick ducks the parts)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Pumping sidechain effect (MASTER > DUCK): every kick from the drum track dips the synth parts, which swell back over an eighth note. About 0.1 KB of flash; has no effect without a drum kick.

items.label: COMP + LIMIT (master compressor, brickwall limiter)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A compressor and a brickwall limiter on the master (GLO > COMP: THRS, RATIO, ATK, REL; GLO > LIMIT: GAIN, CEIL and a GR readout) to glue the mix and keep its peaks under a ceiling; a Comp button and a GR meter in the web mixer. A new project limits at CEIL -3.0 dB (a look-ahead limiter in place of the old one); saved projects keep their own CEIL (OFF: as before). About 2 KB of flash and 2.5 KB of RAM.

items.label: track FILTER (LP <- off -> HP on each track)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A DJ-style filter on each track: FX > FILTER (one knob, FILT: left low-pass, right high-pass, centre off) and FX held + KNOB 4 for the selected track. On the drum track it filters the summed drums and all their sends. Saved with the project, kept when the sound changes, recordable with motion. Costs nothing at the centre; engaged, one filter per track (five on the drum bus).
items.notice: From SLOOP 2.4's track filter by isod89 (isod89/sloop-fm1 v2.4, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: track FILTER: resonance setting (HOME > AUDIO > FILT RESO)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: One setting for every track's FILTER (and the drum track's and the drum lanes'): HOME > AUDIO > FILT RESO, 0 (clean, as before) to 10 (a resonant peak at the cutoff, never self-oscillating). Saved with the project. A few hundred bytes. The master's DJ filter stays clean.
items.notice: From SLOOP 2.8's FILTER RESO by isod89 (isod89/sloop-fm1 b77bf55, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: FOLD insert (wavefolder)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A wavefolder type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: FOLD): the sound driven past full scale folds back, more folds and harmonics as FOLD rises; the drive follows the track's level as DIST's does, the bass stays dry. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Felucca 1.5.6's track INSERT FOLD by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.

items.label: FUZZ insert
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A fuzz type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: FUZZ): a hard-clipped top and a soft, halved bottom (lopsided, buzzy), the drive with FUZZ. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Felucca 1.5.6's track INSERT FUZZ by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.

items.label: PHSR insert (phaser)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A phaser type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: PHSR): four all-pass stages swept slowly (~0.5 Hz); PHSR up to the middle mixes it in, past the middle adds feedback. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Felucca 1.5.6's track INSERT PHASR by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.

items.label: FRMT insert (vowel filter)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A vowel filter type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: FRMT): three formant peaks over the sound; FRMT moves the vowel from A (low) through E, I, O to U (high). 0 is off.
items.notice: From Melodee 1.3.1's FORMANT insert by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0); its vowel table, fixed point here. Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.

items.label: WIDE insert (stereo width)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A stereo width type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: WIDE): one side through slowly swept all-pass filters, the other dry, so a centred mono track spreads out; WIDE sets how much. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Melodee 1.3.1's WIDTH insert by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.

items.label: SFLD insert (sine wavefolder)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A sine wavefolder type (SFLD): like FOLD but the folds are round (a sine of the drive), so it sings and aliases less; soft saturation at first, then more and more folds as SFLD rises. 0 is off.
items.notice: The shape of Felucca 1.5.5's PHASE FOLD by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). On any insert slot (tracks, drum sounds but SUB, drum bus, master, returns). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: RECT insert (rectifier, octave up)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A rectifier type (RECT): up to the middle the wave's lower half is folded up (half-wave, then full-wave: the octave up of an Octavia), past the middle it is driven into a soft clip. 0 is off.
items.notice: On any insert slot (tracks, drum sounds but SUB, drum bus, master, returns). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: HARM insert (harmonic exciter)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A harmonic exciter type (HARM): adds the octave and the twelfth over each note, warm rather than buzzy, more as HARM rises. 0 is off.
items.notice: On any insert slot (tracks, drum sounds but SUB, drum bus, master, returns). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: RING insert (ring modulator)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A ring modulator type (RING): the sound times a sine from 26 Hz (a rough tremolo) to 2.6 kHz (bells, metal), RING picks its pitch. 0 is off.
items.notice: On any insert slot (tracks, drum sounds but SUB, drum bus, master, returns). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: SUB insert (octave down)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: An octave-down type (SUB): a square an octave under the note, following its level, added as SUB rises. For single-note lines (bass, leads): chords give a rough sub. Not on drum sounds. 0 is off.
items.notice: On any insert slot (tracks, drum bus, master, returns). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: SLEW insert (slew-rate crunch)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A slew limiter type (SLEW): the wave can only move so fast, so edges round into ramps, a slow op-amp's dull crunch; light at 1, heavy (muffled, gritty) at 127. 0 is off.
items.notice: On any insert slot (tracks, drum sounds but SUB, drum bus, master, returns). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: TAPE insert (tape tone)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A tape tone type (TAPE): the highs rolled off (from 6.5 kHz at 1 to 1.7 kHz at 127) and the mids moved around at random every couple of seconds, at times inverted against the lows and highs, as a worn tape plays. TAPE sets how far it wanders and how dark it gets. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Melodee 1.3.0's TAPE insert by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0); fixed point here, its RATE and MIX fixed. On the tracks' slots, the drum bus, master, returns and USB input; not on drum sounds (their list is full). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: SPIT insert (random resonant band, driven)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A spitting band type (SPIT): one resonant band jumping at random between 180 Hz and 5.9 kHz a few times a second, driven into a soft clip at the sound's own level and mixed over it. SPIT sharpens the band and the drive. 0 is off.
items.notice: From Melodee 1.3.0's SPIT insert by Kerem Kilic (GPL-3.0); fixed point here, the clip follows the input's level (Melodee's has a fixed ceiling). On the tracks' slots, the drum bus, master, returns and USB input; not on drum sounds (their list is full). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: CHRS insert (chorus copies for the tracks)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: A chorus type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: CHRS), beside the chorus send: two taps around 7 ms swept apart at ~0.8 Hz; CHRS up to the middle mixes it in, past the middle widens the sweep. On the drum track it turns the drums' mid into a stereo chorus. 2 KB of the effects memory an instance. Its line is in the effects memory (below): as many play at once as it holds; a slot that picks it when there is no room left stays dry until some is free (the INSERTS list shows how many more fit). A saved project keeps the type, not the room: on load the slots get it in order T1 T2 T3 DR, the master, the USB input, the returns.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: ECHO insert (short delay copies for the tracks)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: A slapback type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: ECHO), beside the delay send: one repeat 75 ms after the sound; ECHO up to the middle sets its level, past the middle adds repeats (feedback up to 60 %). Up to 93 ms of line an instance (the long, tempo-synced delay stays the send's): 8 KB of the effects memory. Its line is in the effects memory (below): as many play at once as it holds; a slot that picks it when there is no room left stays dry until some is free (the INSERTS list shows how many more fit). A saved project keeps the type, not the room: on load the slots get it in order T1 T2 T3 DR, the master, the USB input, the returns.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: JUNO CHORUS insert (the Juno-106 chorus)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: The Juno-106's chorus as an insert type (INSERTS > S1 / S2, and the master's insert slots: JUNO): the MN3009 BBD model of fm-106, MODE I, II or I+II, JUNO its mix (127: the Juno's chorus on). A mono track comes out stereo. About 130 host instructions a sample an instance; 2 KB of the effects memory. Its line is in the effects memory (below): as many play at once as it holds; a slot that picks it when there is no room left stays dry until some is free (the INSERTS list shows how many more fit). A saved project keeps the type, not the room: on load the slots get it in order T1 T2 T3 DR, the master, the USB input, the returns.
items.notice: From fm-106 by PatttF (GPL-3.0), after Ultramaster KR-106 (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: return feedback sends (B to A, C to A, C to B)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: The master's returns send to the returns on their left too (MASTER > A SENDS, B SENDS, C SENDS: each return to the other two), for feedback between the effects: a delay into a reverb and back. Each such send takes its return's output of the block before (a loop of 32 samples, 0.73 ms), DC-blocked, limited to -12 dBFS and soft-clipped, at a quarter of the gain of a send to the right, so no loop runs away. Without it a return sends only to its right (A to B and C, B to C). About 1.2 KB of RAM; nothing runs while every such send is 0.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: FLNG insert (flanger)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: A flanger type for any insert slot (a track's, the master's, the USB input's) and the returns (FLNG): a short delay swept 0.25 .. 5 ms (~0.25 Hz); FLNG up to the middle mixes it in, past the middle adds feedback. 1 KB of the effects memory an instance. Its line is in the effects memory (below): as many play at once as it holds; a slot that picks it when there is no room left stays dry until some is free (the INSERTS list shows how many more fit). A saved project keeps the type, not the room: on load the slots get it in order T1 T2 T3 DR, the master, the USB input, the returns.
items.notice: From Felucca 1.5.6's track INSERT FLANG by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests and the emulator only, not on a device.

items.label: XDLY insert (LYRA-8 style cross-modulated dual delay)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: Two delay lines whose outputs move each other's time at the audio rate, as the SOMA LYRA-8's modulated delay does (its idea, no code): an insert type for the tracks' slots and the master's (XDLY). Its page has TIME 1 and TIME 2 (each line, 1 ms up to the line's length; turning one bends the repeats), MOD (how far each line's output moves the other's time: a slow chorus to metallic FM grit) and FDBK (the repeats; past ~95 % they grow into a soft clip and sustain, the LYRA's self-oscillation). XDLY, the amount, is the MIX, 0 off. A mono track gets the two lines' mean, the drum bus and the master line 1 on L and line 2 on R. A track's repeats go on after its notes end. About 190 host instructions a sample an instance. Each instance is two lines of the length below in the effects memory (64 KB, or 32 KB); as many play at once as it holds, a slot picking it when there is no room left stays dry.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: XDLY line length (its longest TIME)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: How long each of XDLY's two lines is: TIME's top end. The shorter line halves every TIME and takes 32 KB less of the effects memory an instance.

items.label: effects memory (shared by the delay and every insert with a line)
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: One pool memory, in 1 KB units, for the delay send's line (its length above) and the line of every insert that has one: CHRS 2 KB, ECHO 8 KB, JUNO CHORUS 2 KB, FLNG 1 KB, XDLY 2 lines of its length. An insert takes its room when a slot picks it and gives it back when the slot lets go; with no room left the slot shows FULL and stays dry. How many of each play at once is what this memory holds: the builder's notice says, for each type built, up to how many at once (alone) in the size chosen, and how many more while the delay or the chorus is in no master slot: a send in none lends its line to the inserts (as many as fit; taken back, faded out, when the send is put back). Auto: the delay's line plus one line of each insert built, so every insert built can play at least once at the same time. Larger: more at once. At least the delay's line, and room for one line of each insert built (an error names the one that does not fit).
choices: auto: the delay's line and one line of each insert

items.label: GATER insert (tempo-synced trance gate)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: A rhythmic volume gate type for the tracks' insert slots (INSERTS > S1 / S2: GATER), locked to the tempo and the sequencer's steps (it restarts with PLAY, follows the swing): one of 16 built-in 16-step patterns (trance gates, 1/8 and 1/16 chops, offbeats, dotted, clave), a RATE of 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 or their triplets, DEPTH (the amount: how far a closed step closes, 0 off) and SHAPE (hard to smooth). Every track can run it at once.
items.notice: Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: CHORD+ (black keys change the chord), STRUM, VLEAD
items.desc: With a chord mode on (SCL > CHORD), the black keys change the chord played: F# major <-> minor, G# adds the 7th, A# sus4, C# the 9th, D# inverts; hold several to combine, or press one while a chord is held. SCL 2 gains STRUM (1-60 ms a note, right low to high, left high to low; keys and chord steps) and VLEAD (each chord voiced nearest the last). Recorded as it sounds; MIDI out sends the chord unstrummed.
items.notice: From SLOOP 2.4's CHORD+ by isod89 (isod89/sloop-fm1 v2.4, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: song sections
items.desc: 8 / 16: banks of 4 (SAVE + OCT), stored compressed in one 32 KiB log with a MEM gauge; the old slots move in at the first start. 4: the slots as before (needed by motion recording)

items.label: snapshots (whole-state slots)
items.desc: PROJECT > SNAPSHOT: the working project, every section and the song in one slot, loaded back whole (the state before is kept in BEFORE LOAD); export / import in the web editor. The flash comes from the end of USR3 (slots + 4 sectors of 4 KiB): the user sample slot USR3 holds that much less (docs/SNAPSHOTS.md)

items.label: per-project patterns and scenes
items.desc: Each of the 16 projects owns its state, 16 patterns a track, its scenes A..P and its song (docs/PROJECTS-DESIGN.md): nothing done in one project touches another. The log moves to 0xA0000 and grows to 128 KB (80 KB with SAMPLE or DRUM_USR built: user sample slot 1, which the samples lose). The old log at 0x97000 is not read. LFO held: the PATTERN layer (launch at the end, the next bar or now; store, copy, clear); the web editor shows the slots in the mixer. Off: a project is a plain section with its steps in it, in the old log.

items.label: undo / redo history (many levels)
items.desc: Undo and redo of pattern edits (EDIT + OCT- / OCT+) over many levels; the history lives in the pool and RAM this build leaves free (at least 1 KiB). About 2.2 KB of flash; off: a single undo level.

items.label: performance macros (GLO > MACRO)
items.desc: COLOR, MOTION, SPACE, ENERGY: four knobs, each moving several sounds' parameters at once (filters and FM index, LFO depths, sends and width, drive and drum level), kept per project and section (the drum track's unused ENV / LFO DEST values: no format change); recorded by motion recording. At home: no change. About 1.4 KB of flash and 0.4 KB of RAM.

items.label: ENERGY bands thin / thicken the drums
items.desc: ENERGY also thins or thickens the drum pattern in five bands, walked on the beat: core lanes on the eighths, no ghosts, as written, harder hits, hat ratchets and a snare fill every second pass. About 0.6 KB of flash.

items.label: REC plain: every note played is recorded, the voice mode never cuts it
items.desc: Experimental (2026-10-21, off for now). Recording keeps every note you play: a chord stays a chord, an overdub only touches a note you play again, and a long note you play into keeps going. The voice mode (MONO, LEGATO, UNISON) decides only what the voice plays, as it does for the keys, instead of cutting a recorded step to one note and joining the notes held over each other. A part on an engine that is mono by nature (ACID) records as before; an arp part always records plain. About 0.1 KB of flash less or more.

items.label: note generators (STEP's GEN and GEN OUT)
items.desc: A note generator on every synth track and every drum lane, played live over the pattern and never written into it but by WRITE, which asks: EUCLID (HITS spread over STEPS, turned by ROT), RANDOM (DENSITY, SEED, ACCENT) and PULSE (EVERY, OFFSET, RATCHET), each REPLACING, ADDING to or MASKING the pattern. STEP's last pages GEN and GEN OUT; saved with the project, one undo level a WRITE. On a drum lane picked with ALGORITHM, that lane only. Apart from the STEP tools (SEQTOOLS) and from GRIDS (GEN_GRIDS) since 2026-10-22: each builds without the others. EUCLID after Felucca 1.5.6's. About 6.8 KB of flash and 2 KB of RAM: 6.1 KB of it the generators' framework, shared with GRIDS, EUCLID RANDOM PULSE themselves 0.7 KB (the builder's measure, 2026-10-22).

items.label: USB MIDI (always: notes, clock, the editor, updates)
items.desc: USB MIDI is in every build: notes and clock both ways, the web editor, and firmware updates (the installer and the builder flash through it). Shown for the record, it cannot be switched off.

items.label: USB serial console (logs, diagnostics)
items.desc: A read-only serial console on the USB port, next to USB MIDI: the logs and the diagnostic commands (with Bluetooth audio, its btinq / btpage traces). Not with USB audio: the USB port has three data endpoints, USB MIDI takes one and USB audio the other two.

items.label: USB audio (4 stems in, stereo out)
items.desc: 4 stems in + stereo out (UAC1) next to USB MIDI; the stems are resampled to the computer's clock (cubic, after X0X 80b7d40), so a host passing the input live to an output does not drop out. Needs +12 KB pool (a resampler in the audio path is CPU-heavy). It streams on the FM-1 since 2026-10-12 (before, a USB audio build hung and went to the USB rescue); its audio quality is not checked yet. Not with the serial console: the USB port has three data endpoints, USB MIDI takes one and USB audio the other two.
items.notice: USB audio capture resampler ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0), 80b7d40.

items.label: TRS MIDI IN
items.desc: MIDI input on the TRS jack (notes and clock from a keyboard or sequencer). About 0.6 KB of flash; off: the jack hears nothing, and SYNC TRS has no clock.

items.label: MIDI clock in + out
items.desc: MIDI clock both ways. In: follow an external MIDI clock and start / stop (GLO > SYSTEM SYNC: AUTO takes the TRS jack, else USB, else the internal tempo). Out: send MIDI clock on USB so a computer, drum machine or sequencer can follow the FM-1: 24 ticks a beat (also while stopped, so the other side has the tempo first), Start, Stop, and Song Position + Continue when the FM-1 itself continues an external song. Each tick leaves with the sound of its beat (latency-compensated, no jitter of its own), follows tempo changes and the nudge, and never swings. Switched on in the HOME menu (CLOCK OUT, off by default). While the FM-1 follows a USB clock nothing is sent back to USB; following the TRS jack, the clock is passed on to USB. The TRS jack is input only (no MIDI out on the FM-1's board). Off: the FM-1 always runs on its own tempo and sends no clock.

items.label: MIDI expression (bend, mod, sustain, RPN)
items.desc: Plays more than notes from MIDI: pitch bend, mod wheel, breath, foot, aftertouch, sustain pedal and pitch-bend range (RPN 0). About 0.5 KB of flash; off: only notes and the panic messages work.

items.label: MIDI note out of the sequencer (GLOBAL MIDI OUT = BOTH or SEQ)
items.desc: MIDI OUT = BOTH (SLOOP 2.4's SEQ: the keys and the sequencer) or SEQ (the sequencer alone, no keys): what the sequencer, the arp and the rolls play also goes to MIDI out, each track on its channel, every note ended (STOP, a channel changed, back to KEYS). Switched on GLOBAL's MIDI page (MIDI OUT KEYS / BOTH / SEQ). About 1.2 to 2.5 KB of flash, by build; off: the line goes and only the panel's keys go out.

items.label: say what a project uses and this build lacks
items.desc: 'MISSING: PHYS T2, KIT 909' in the top bar when a project, song section, user preset or kit uses an engine, kit, sample set or FX this build leaves out (once per item until power-off; never stalls the audio); PROJECT > TOOLS > MISSING lists them again. Off: they play their stand-ins silently (saves 1.5 KB of flash)

items.label: favorites: mark sounds, browse only them
items.desc: With the presets: SHIFT2 (OCT+ held) + PRESETS marks the sound playing, SHIFT2 + SELECT browses only the favorites, a star after a favorite's name in the toast and in PROJECT > USER (SHIFT2 + ITEM marks a slot). Up to 64 factory sounds (kept by engine and name: they stay marked over builds that leave engines out) and any of the 32 user presets (an erased preset loses its mark); the FM6 / CZ banks and the drum track have none. Kept with the settings (136 B at the end of the settings record: an older record reads whole with none; a build without this item keeps the rest and forgets them on its next save). About 1 KB of flash, 136 B of pool. Off: no marks.
items.notice: After Felucca 1.6's favorites by Leo Kuroshita (GPL-3.0). Tested in the host UI and storage tests only, not on a device.

items.label: help line: what the knob changes, in words
items.desc: the screen's last line names what a knob changes in plain words, e.g. 'Filter cutoff', 'Reverb send', while a value turns and ~2 s after, and always on GLOBAL, SYSTEM and PROJECT (the cursor line, the hot action, ' -> SAVE' after an action that asks first: the button that runs it); only the lines of the features built (tools/param_help.json, also the web editor's tooltips). About 7.7 KB of flash (the texts packed), no RAM code

items.label: SYSTEM's debug pages (internals, USB stats)
items.desc: SYSTEM keeps its pages for finding faults: INTERNALS (the last reset, the flash's interrupts-off time, the second core's internals), USB STATS (the USB audio glitch counters) and on INFO the clock, the second core, the drops and the CPU guard apart. Off: INFO shows what a player wants, CPU LOAD, UNDERRUNS (the drop-outs counted in) and BATTERY, in the large face, and the code of the rest is left out (about 2.9 KB less flash, measured on a USB-audio build). The red / amber mark on the header's rule after a drop-out stays either way.

items.label: knob acceleration by turn speed
items.desc: 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 / 8 steps a detent when turned fast; never on lists (engines, kits, presets)
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0): knob acceleration. Tested in the emulator only.

items.label: screen data speed (SPI clock)
items.desc: How fast data is sent to the display: 60 MHz / (n + 1). Faster redraws finish sooner (less tearing); the ST7789V takes ~62 MHz, so 60 MHz is the limit. No flash cost; the faster settings are untested here on hardware.
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0): the faster LCD clock ran on X0X's FM-1; untested on hardware here.

items.label: screen: send only the changed rectangle
items.desc: Redraws only the part of the graph strip that changed instead of the whole strip: less data per frame and less tearing (with the 30 MHz screen clock). Costs about 1.5 KB of flash and 0.6 KB of RAM.
items.notice: Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0): dirty-rectangle screen updates. Not yet tried on hardware here.

items.label: web editor (USB SysEx)
items.desc: The web editor's communication layer: the frames and INFO, BUILD, PING. What it can do comes with its options: BACKUP, LIBRARIAN, live editing (ED_LIVE) and its features. Firmware updates (the installer, M-UPGRADE) and the USB rescue are not part of it: every build has them.
items.off_warning: without it there is no web editor (so no backup / restore from it); installing and the USB rescue still work

items.label: backup / restore from the web editor
items.desc: everything in flash to one .optimist-backup file and back (editor cmds 43..48; without live editing the sample slots' 11..15 and the snapshots' 54..57 too, which a restore writes through); a restore onto another build reports what it skips and what plays a stand-in
items.off_warning: no backup: export projects and kits one by one before an update

items.label: web editor: librarian (projects, presets, patterns, kits)
items.desc: The web editor manages the user data one piece at a time: the user presets (the Library: list, rename, move, erase, files) and the user drum kits (load, store, erase, files), with live editing or without; without it also the sections A..P (load, save, a file each) and the per-track patterns (copy, clear, files), next to Backup. Editor cmds 16..21, 38..41; without live editing 9 and 79..84 too (editor/ed_lite.c).
items.off_warning: no user presets or user kits from the web editor (the device's own SAVE pages keep them)

items.label: web editor: live editing (else backup / restore and the librarian)
items.desc: The web editor edits the FM-1 live: the sounds' values, presets, user presets, tracks, steps, the mixer, kits and the ED_* pages, kept in sync both ways. Off: the editor's side is backup and restore only (the frames, INFO, BUILD, the user sample slots a restore writes, the snapshots, cmds 43..48: editor/ed_lite.c); the web page then shows its Backup (and, with LIBRARIAN, the librarian) alone. The ED_* items do nothing without it.
items.off_warning: no live editing from the web editor: backup and restore, and with LIBRARIAN the projects, presets, patterns and kits

items.label: web editor: the mixer (effect slots, drum lanes, solo and mute)
items.desc: The web editor's mixer beyond levels and pans: every FX slot by owner with its parameters (track inserts, the drum bus and lane inserts, master inserts, returns, the USB input; cmds 86, 87, 94), the drum lanes' pan, mutes, solos and LFOs (cmd 95), track and lane SOLO and MUTE (cmd 104). Off: the editor's Inserts / Returns pop-ups and FX pages, the lane LFOs and the strips' SOLO are not offered; the levels, pans and sends stay.

items.label: web editor: the sequencer (lane steps, pattern tools, song chain)
items.desc: The web editor's sequencer tools beyond the steps themselves: a step held in a drum lane's context with the device's own list of lockable values (cmd 105; with the automation store), the pattern tools REVERSE, RANDOM, COOK, LENGTH and the note generators run by the device (cmd 98; SEQTOOLS, NOTEGEN), the song chain (cmd 97; the arranger). Off: the editor lists raw parameter ids, has no tools buttons and no song chain.

items.label: web editor: the device's screens (cards, GLOBAL / SYSTEM, scope)
items.desc: The web editor's Device tab: the Optimist UI's SOUND, MIX, MASTER, PROJECT, STEPS, SONG and TEMPO pages as rows of cards (cmd 99), GLOBAL and SYSTEM as the device's lines with their help (cmd 96) and the oscilloscope (cmd 101). Off: no Device tab; the editor keeps its own Sound / Mixer / Sequence tabs.

items.label: web editor: the screen mirrored (the Mirror tab, the iPhone app; USB or Bluetooth)
items.desc: The FM-1's screen in the web editor's Mirror tab or on an iPhone (the Optimist Mirror app, ios/OptimistMirror), over a USB cable or Bluetooth MIDI (with BLE): while one asks (cmd 106), every write to the panel also goes out, run-length coded, as it is drawn, so it shows the very pixels: the mixer, the step grid, the layers, the dialogs. No frame buffer on the device; nothing is sent while none asks; the mixer's meters go 10 times a second over USB, never over Bluetooth. A link that falls behind (USB: the host stops reading; Bluetooth: its 8 KB send ring is full) drops what is drawn and catches up once it is clear again, at most 4 times a second: the panel's bands drawn again in place, no flash on the device. Over Bluetooth whole screens come at the rate the radio carries. With live editing (ED_LIVE) or without.
items.tested: host-tested only (the stream decoded back to every screen drawn, every catch-up the panel), not on a device

items.label: sound tables and FM6 buffers in the pool, not main RAM
items.desc: Moves what the sound loops read from main RAM to the pool: the sine, soft-clip and GRAIN window tables (about 2.5 KB, copied there from flash at start-up) and FM6's sine table, operator buses and voices (about 5.9 KB), so builder items get that much more main RAM. Unverified on hardware: both are the same SRAM as far as is known and the emulator cannot tell a speed difference, so on the FM-1 it may be slower; compare the console's TABBENCH figures and the CPU meter with it off and on. The sound is the same.

items.label: tables unpacked into RAM (flash for pool)
items.group: FX: any number (each track its own)
items.desc: Trades flash for pool: smooth lookup tables the sound and the UI read are kept in flash as the differences between neighbours and unpacked at start-up into the pool, always the pool whether or not TAB_IN_POOL is on (main RAM pays nothing); the undo history ring, which takes what the pool has left, is that much shorter. The same values: the sound and the screens are unchanged; the tables read a little faster from RAM than from flash. The eleven small tables (pitch, envelope and LFO rates, cutoff, levels, decay): 4.3 KB of pool for about 2.2 KB of flash; every table adds FM6's five (fine, detune, LFO and portamento): 7.3 KB of pool for about 3.1 KB of flash (measured on the synth profile and the user's). With PLAITS built, either choice also unpacks its five waveshapers: 2.5 KB more of pool for about 1.9 KB more of flash. Either choice also moves the small font's bitmaps to the pool as they are (1.5 KB of pool for 1.0 KB of flash: they travel in the start-up stream like the rest) and, when built, JUNO's eleven small tables, the master compressor's 2^x curve and XDLY's TIME curve, delta-coded like the small tables (together 2.0 KB of pool for 1.3 KB of flash on the user's configuration, 2026-10-24).
choices: the small tables and the small font; PLAITS' waveshapers, JUNO's tables, the compressor's and XDLY's curves when built (5.8 KB of pool, up to 11.4 with every one)
every table, FM6's five too (3 KB of pool more)
items.tested: host-tested only (tests/tab_coded_test.c: every table decoded byte for byte), not on a device

items.label: save while playing (flash writes in short windows)
items.desc: Saving no longer stops or waits for the transport: SAVE on a user preset, a kit, a project, a name or the song writes as the music plays (no STOP BEFORE SAVE, the naming page no longer stops and restarts the transport), and what waited for the stop (live sections and patterns, the song, the settings) goes to flash while playing, one record at a time, 250 ms apart, once the panel has rested 1.5 s. The audio keeps playing because every sector erase is already cut into 1 ms windows with the erase suspended between them (hal/fm1_flash_slice.h); the main loop (the screen, the panel) still pauses for one record's write, tens of ms. If the flash part ever holds an erase in one window (no suspend: the audio silenced in it), saves wait for the stop again until the next start. Snapshots, backup restores, sample uploads, the web editor's writes and the working project's autosave still wait for the stop. About 240 B of flash, 1 byte of RAM.
items.off_warning: saves refused (STOP BEFORE SAVE) or held until the transport stops, as before
items.tested: built and host-tested only, not on a device

items.label: predictive CPU guard (ease back before shedding)
items.desc: Avoids audio dropouts under heavy load by easing quality back step by step before cutting notes. Under overload (the measured load or the one predicted from the voices sounding, over 85 % for 8 halves, or a late half): first ACID without oversampling and ANALOG 2's swarm at 2 copies, then UNISON at 2 voices, then voices shed, never the bass or the lead (MONO / LEGATO / UNISON parts) nor the drums; back after 2 s under 80 % counting what each step saved; SYSTEM > INFO's GUARD line (SYS_DEBUG) shows the step. Weights: tools/builder/cpu_costs.py from tests/cpu_baseline.txt (docs/CPU-GUARD.md)

items.label: voices: reuse a track's own released voice before taking another's
items.desc: When every voice is in use and a track plays a new note, it first restarts one of its own voices that is already releasing, instead of fading out another track's tail. The other tracks keep their tails, and no extra fading voice runs for a moment over the budget. When the track has no releasing voice, the voice is taken from another track as before. A few dozen bytes.
items.notice: From JIANT 0.9.9 cpu3 by juanjiant-bit (juanjiant-bit/JIANT da61bc62, GPL-3.0). Tested in the host tests only, not on a device.

items.label: more memory from the data cache (for the undo history)
items.desc: Uses 2, 4 or 7 of the 8 data-cache ways (4 KB each) as RAM; 7 is what M-VAVE's own FM-1 firmware and the AC79 SDK's flash-only builds do; the instruction cache (the flash's code and constants) keeps all its ways. The memory is tested at start-up; when the test passes it becomes the undo history's second part (28 KB instead of what main RAM has left), else everything is put back as it was and nothing uses it. It costs about 0.4 KB of flash and 0.1 KB of fast RAM code. Off until checked on an FM-1: whether the flash's data reads use the data cache (then the sound's tables in flash could cost CPU) is not known; the console's tabbench (flash 16K) and boot lines show it.
items.tested: on one FM-1 2026-10-18: the boot test passes, cache RAM as fast as main RAM, but flash data reads over 16 KB 57x slower (1.7 us vs 32 ns: flash data goes through the data cache, 4 KB left)

items.label: hand-written assembly speed-ups (FM6, ANALOG 2)
items.desc: The hottest loops of FM6 and ANALOG 2 written in the processor's assembly: the same sound, about 8 to 19 % less audio CPU (emulator), for about 0.6 KB of flash and 0.7 KB of fast RAM code. Keep on; off only to compare with the plain C.

items.label: second CPU core renders parts 2-3
items.desc: The FM-1's second CPU core renders synth parts 2 and 3 while the first renders the rest, cutting the first core's load by 40 to 44 % in the emulator, with the same sound. It costs about 3.3 KB of flash, 3.7 KB of RAM and 6 KB of pool. On some FM-1s the second core misreads RAM at the boot loader's supply: it then runs nothing it misread, is held for the session and the FM-1 goes on with one core (the message CPU1 OFF MISREAD); a boot after one that crashed in its first 30 s stays on one core.
items.notice: Its guard against misread RAM is ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0): the second core runs only the next job, with a matching check word, and is held at the first one it refuses.
items.tested: on the FM-1: the default since 2026-10-16

items.label: raise the core rails to the FM-1's stock values at start-up (for the second core)
items.desc: At start-up, before the second core, the audio and Bluetooth, the FM-1's rails are set as its own M-VAVE firmware sets them: the 1.4 V rail moved from its LDO to the DC-DC, then raised to 1.60 V (VDC14 7), then the core rail to 1.38 V (SYSVDD 15), a step at a time, never lowered (the boot loader leaves 1.40 V and 1.26 V). Read back after: if a value is wrong, the second core stays off (2ND CORE OFF SUPPLY) and the FM-1 runs on one core. SYSTEM > INTERNALS shows the rails (SUPPLY). Second-core builds only; it replaces the earlier DUAL_BOOST (1.50 V / 1.38 V on the LDO). On the second core's test unit both cores crashed within seconds at the boot loader's rails and ran 3 x 3 minutes with 1.50 V / 1.38 V; the stock sequence itself is still being measured.
items.notice: At your own risk: the FM-1's own firmware raises its rails this way, every custom firmware leaves them at the boot loader's lower levels. 1.38 V core and 1.60 V on the 1.4 V rail are above the AC79 datasheet's table (the chip's absolute limits are not public); chips vary from unit to unit; the effect on heat and battery life has not been measured.
items.tested: the sequence emulator- and host-tested; 1.50 V / 1.38 V measured on one FM-1 (2026-10-16)

items.label: Bluetooth LE MIDI, our own stack
items.desc: BLE MIDI as the stock firmware offers it (named Optimist XXXX, the BLE-MIDI service), from a stack written for Optimist (docs/BLE-STACK.md): BLE in plays the synth, the FM-1's own notes go out with real timestamps. Tested on an FM-1 with macOS Audio MIDI Setup (not yet with iOS or Windows). The radio's start-up tables, captured from the stock V15 firmware, are included: no V15 file is needed (FM1_STOCK_FWSC makes a fresh capture instead, with the same result). Bluetooth starts OFF: switch it on in SYSTEM > Bluetooth. About 32 KB of flash and 6.5 KB of RAM (the menu shows the measured figures; BLE_DIAG below adds more); where the build then overflows, ticking it removes the smallest single item that frees enough (sample sets first, then other items), or the one you pick instead.
items.tested: tested on an FM-1 with macOS Audio MIDI Setup, not yet with iOS or Windows

items.label: BLE diagnostics: the console's blell, counters and rings
items.desc: For finding BLE faults: the console's blell command (needs the serial console, USB_CONSOLE) and the counters and rings behind it (link-layer events, the radio's receive and transmit state, the protocol packets, BLE-MIDI in). About 6 KB of flash and 2.3 KB of RAM, and 6 KB of flash more with the console (USB_CONSOLE) for blell itself. Leave it off for normal use: BLE works the same without it; bletrim and blevm stay, and so does the boot breadcrumb.

items.label: BLE pairing when a Mac or phone connects to the FM-1 (Just Works, encrypted, remembered)
items.desc: LE legacy pairing with Just Works (no passkey, as the FM-1 has no screen keypad for it) and bonding, so a Mac or phone that pairs once gets an encrypted link and finds the FM-1 bonded after a power-off. The FM-1 hands out its identity and takes the other side's (its IRK and identity address, kept until power-off for now), which reconnecting to devices with private addresses needs later. Pairing happens only when the other side asks for it. Paired with a Mac on an FM-1 (2026-10-18). About 3.6 KB of flash and 0.4 KB of RAM.
items.tested: on an FM-1 with a Mac (2026-10-18)

items.label: BLE devices: the FM-1 connects to BLE-MIDI devices
items.desc: SYSTEM > BT MIDI lists the BLE-MIDI devices nearby (keyboards, controllers, a Mac or an iPhone app that advertises BLE MIDI, another FM-1), scanning while the page is on screen with no link (the FM-1 stops advertising meanwhile). Picking one connects to it as a central, MIDI both ways; it becomes the last device, which the FM-1 reconnects to by itself while Bluetooth is on (with up to 3 others remembered). Two levels, for the flash they take: FULL (1) pairs when the other side asks, with Just Works or, for an iPhone app that needs it, a 6-digit code shown on the FM-1, and finds the last device again when its address changes (Macs and iPhones use private addresses): everything works, 21.9 KB of flash and 2.3 KB of RAM. MINIMAL (3) never pairs: controllers and another FM-1 work; a device that asks to pair (a Mac or an iPhone app advertising BLE MIDI, as Apple's do, some controllers) fails with FAILED: NEEDS PAIRING: 13.4 KB and 1.6 KB (8.5 KB of flash less than FULL). Level 1 brings the bonding of BLE_BOND with it; at level 3 BLE_BOND still lets a Mac pair with the FM-1 when the Mac connects to it.
choices: full: also pairs with devices that ask (passkey, private addresses)
items.tested: on an FM-1: an iPhone app reconnected as the last device (2026-10-18)

items.label: Bluetooth Classic Audio (A2DP Source, SBC)
items.desc: Bluetooth Classic audio out (A2DP source, SBC 44.1 kHz) to headphones and speakers: its own page, SYSTEM > BT AUDIO (MODE OFF, MAN, AUTO), beside BT MIDI: with BLE built, MIDI and audio can be on at the same time on the one radio. Our own stack: inquiry, paging, Secure Simple Pairing (Just Works), E0 encryption, L2CAP, AVDTP and a fixed-point SBC encoder. Streams on the FM-1 to AirPods, a Sony WH-1000XM4 and a Bose SoundLink Mini (2026-10-23).
items.notice: experimental: Bluetooth Classic A2DP audio source
items.tested: host-tested (SSP, SAFER+, SBC encoder, AVDTP, L2CAP) and unit-tested

items.label: Bluetooth audio: adaptive frequency hopping (the channels the headset fails on skipped)
items.desc: What every phone's Bluetooth controller does: the FM-1 counts the headset's answers per radio channel (79 of them) every 30 s and takes the channels it fails on out of the hopping (LMP_set_AFH; at least 20 stay), so a few bad channels no longer stall the stream. Measured need and result (2026-10-23, a WH-1000XM4): as the FM-1 warmed, channels 7 MHz apart went deaf (a clock harmonic's comb) and the stream stalled and crackled on them; with this on, 6 channels dropped over 6 minutes, every switch held and not one audio packet was lost. A console build (BT_DIAG) switches only when told (btpage afh=0 / 1 / 3).

items.label: Bluetooth audio diagnostics: the console's btrx / bttrace, counters and logs
items.desc: For finding Bluetooth audio faults on a console build (USB_CONSOLE): the btrx and bttrace logs, the status histograms and the per-second counters (receive status bits, signal level, gain), and the live btpage pll= / agc= / follow= commands, and every line the Bluetooth stack writes to the console (btinq, btpage). About 14 KB of flash and 6.4 KB of RAM with the console. Leave it off for normal use: the audio works the same without it.

items.label: per-step chance (STEP 2 PROB)
items.desc: Gives each synth step a chance to play (SEQ > STEP 2, KNOB 2: 0 to 100 % in 5 % steps); a step that fails plays as a rest. About 0.5 KB of flash; nothing changes until a step's chance is turned down. Synth tracks only; the web editor does not show it yet. Off: every step plays (chances stay saved).
items.provenance_line: hugelton/Felucca @ 727f272 (Felucca 1.0 source) by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: keys light the notes played
items.desc: Lights the keys of the notes the selected track plays (its steps, the arpeggiator, held notes), so you see the pattern on the keyboard. About 0.2 KB of flash, LEDs only; with LIGHTS, MENU > NOTES turns it on and off at run time.
items.provenance_line: hugelton/Felucca @ 20c275e (Felucca 1.0.1, #38) by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: SCL > QNT SEQ (sequenced notes snap)
items.desc: SCL > QNT SEQ: the keys and the sequenced notes snap to the scale as they play, so a pattern follows a change of ROOT or SCALE; the steps keep their notes as written. About 0.3 KB of flash; not on GM KIT or SLICE parts. A build without it plays a project's QNT SEQ as ALL.
items.provenance_line: hugelton/Felucca @ 20c275e (Felucca 1.0.1, #37) by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: reverb: SPRING
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: A spring-tank reverb, one of the reverb's algorithms: the chirp and drip of a guitar amp's spring (SPRNG on FX > REVERB > TYPE when two or more are ticked). Its output is mono, and it is a little lighter on CPU than ROOM (emulator). Beside ROOM: about 1.9 KB of flash and 2.3 KB of RAM; ticked alone it is the only reverb.
items.provenance_line: hugelton/Felucca @ 727f272 (Felucca 1.0 source) by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: BASS+ speaker mode
items.group: FX: limited instances (once, or a set count)
items.desc: A third MENU > LOWCUT setting (OFF / LOWCUT / BASS+) for the FM-1's small speaker: it adds harmonics of the bass below ~150 Hz, which the speaker can play, and raises the low cut to ~220 Hz. About 0.5 KB of flash and 0.35 KB of RAM; CPU only while BASS+ is on.
items.provenance_line: hugelton/Felucca @ 727f272 (Felucca 1.0 source) by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: screen brightness (MENU > BRIGHT)
items.desc: MENU > BRIGHT: the screen backlight in 8 levels, 4/16 at the lowest (software PWM). The level lasts until power-off: every boot starts at full and a dim level is never saved. About 36 B of flash; X0X reports it working on a real FM-1. Off: always full brightness.
items.notice: This backlight PWM froze an FM-1 at its lowest level on X0X (issue #2; the backlight line also enables the key matrix, which this build keeps enabled during each scan). Optimist boots at full brightness every time, never stores a dim level and never goes below 4/16, so a power-off always brings the screen back at full. Ported from X0X by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0).
items.provenance_line: charlesvestal/fm1-x0x @ 61654ba (Knob acceleration by speed, screen brightness, ...) by Charles Vestal (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: motion recording (knobs per step)
items.desc: Motion recording: while recording, knob turns are stored per step and replayed on every pass (SEQ > MOTION: play on / off per track, clear). The events are the automation store's (up to 128 a track with its locks, nudges and fills); undone with the recording pass, editable from the web editor's protocol (AUTO_GET / AUTO_SET). About 3.4 KB of flash, 0.5 KB of RAM and 1.4 KB of pool (measured before the automation store).
items.provenance_line: hugelton/Felucca @ 727f272 (Felucca 1.0 source) by Leo Kuroshita (@kurogedelic), Hügelton Instruments (GPL-3.0-only)

items.label: PHYS (physical models)
items.desc: Physical-modelling engine (engine 11): modal, string, membrane and sympathetic-string models, 3 voices per part. Heavy: about 9.8 KB of flash and 38.7 KB of pool, and 3 voices of its heaviest preset take about 17 % of the audio budget at 312 MHz (at 96 MHz that was too much and voices were shed).

items.label: note generator GRIDS (Mutable Instruments Grids)
items.desc: Mutable Instruments Grids (Emilie Gillet) as a drum note generator: 25 drum patterns on a 5 x 5 map, read between them at X and Y. On DR itself (no lane picked) STEP has GRIDS (X, Y, CHAOS) and DENSITY (BD, SD, HH) in GEN's place: one GRIDS for the kit, playing the first KICK lane, the first SNARE lane and the CLOSED HAT lane, and the ACCENT lane where a part plays HARD; GEN OUT turns it on and WRITEs it. Its six values are the drum track's own, saved with the project and recorded as motion. CHAOS is Grids' random push, new each bar. On a picked lane (or T1 T2 T3) GRIDS is a GEN TYPE (X, Y, DENS) playing the part of the lane's sound. One bar of 16ths, repeated through LEN. Builds STEP's GEN and GEN OUT pages itself, with or without the other generators (NOTEGEN: EUCLID, RANDOM, PULSE); alone, GRIDS is the one TYPE. About 8.7 KB of flash and 2 KB of RAM alone: 6.1 KB of it the generators' framework, shared with NOTEGEN, and 1.2 KB the map; 2.5 KB more next to NOTEGEN (the builder's measure, 2026-10-22).

items.label: GRIDS: Euclidean mode (OUT EUCL)
items.desc: Grids' second output mode for the kit's GRIDS: EUCLIDEAN. GRIDS gets an OUT card (DRUMS / EUCL); in EUCL the three parts play Euclidean rhythms instead of the drum map, as Grids does: X, Y and CHAOS set the kick's, the snare's and the hat's lengths (1 to 32 steps), DENSITY's BD, SD and HH how many of their steps hit, spread as evenly as they go (Grids' own table, worked out the same way). Each part runs on its own length through the passes, against the pattern's LEN. No accent in this mode, as on Grids. OUT is saved with the project; a build without this item plays DRUMS. About 1 KB of flash.

GRIDS plays the values moved, step by step; the values you set stay as they are. Each LFO restarts at PLAY, as a lane's does. Saved with the project; a build without this item plays the values as set. Needs the drum editor (DRUM_EDIT: the lanes' LFOs). About 0.7 KB of flash.

items.label: GRIDS: velocity (VEL on DENSITY)
items.desc: The kit GRIDS' hits play at their own dynamic: Grids' drum map gives every step a level, and the level picks the hit's velocity, so the main beats play loud and the in-between ones soft or as ghosts, into the drum sounds and MIDI out. As the drum steps keep it: four dynamics (GHOST, SOFT, NORM, HARD), so STEP draws them and WRITE keeps them. A VEL card on DENSITY turns it ON / OFF (OFF: as before, HARD where Grids' accent would be); saved with the project. DRUMS mode only (EUCL has no levels). About 0.2 KB of flash.
